chapter: Road bands: Hucklebuck Williams and Tiny Bradshaw
title: Leaving Florida with Paul "Hucklebuck" Williams's band
summary: Sam takes the first band through needing a bass player, Hucklebuck Williams's, and describes its musicians and the midget dancer.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: He said, "anytime you get ready to come." I said, "well, I'm ready now." So he said, "I'll send you a ticket. So I caught the Silver Meteor. My bass, bags, and he met me at the station down there, man. No-no--no--
I'm going too fast. I'm going too fast. I left Florida with Paul "Hucklebuck" Williams.

That's wh it was. Came up. Then I was-- that was around--gigging around Miami Beach was different. Working with different bands. After working in nightclubs in Miami Beach, you know, wasn't doing all that much. Came around there so I said the first band come through here that needs a bass player, I'm going. That's what happened. And Paul "Hucklebuck" Williams came through there, needed a bass player.

Cause their bass player had quit or something. I don't know what it was. And somebody told them about me and they called me up. And I say "shit, yeah." I'm ready to go. I got on the bus and left with Paul "Hucklebuck" Williams. OK. Now everybody in Paul Williams band is--is--is--raw men. I met a little young dude--I don't know nothing, bout nothing. All I know, I'm on this bus, I'm working my way back up to New York. We're playing all through the South. And strangely enough, man, this man had a fine band, man.
And a good book, you know.
Lee Polk. Lee Anderson. All these guys in the band, man.
The only thing that I didn't like with this-- with that--was that--that fucking midget they had back there. Called it 'Hucklebuck,' you know.
The little midget they carried--to do--the 'Hucklebuck.' You know, they had a little midget, a little dude.
